Petitioners file notice to challenge Appeals Court verdict restoring NG-CDF at the Supreme Court

about.text: The National Government Constituencies Development Fund (NG-CDF) is established by section 4 of the NG-CDF Act, No. 30 of 2015. Section 4(1)(a) provides that the Fund consists of 'not less than 2.5% (two and half percentum) of all the national government's share of revenue as divided by the annual Division of Revenue Act'. Section 4(3) provides that the amount in a year shall not be less than the previous year's appropriation unless otherwise allowed by the Act. (Act PDF p.7)

Allocation formula (section 34): each constituency's budget ceiling is three quarters of the Fund divided equally among all constituencies, plus one quarter divided among constituencies taking into account the number of wards in each, subject to the emergency reserve (s.8) and the Board's running costs (s.23(1), capped at 5% of the Fund). The Board allocates funds to every constituency each year with the approval of the relevant National Assembly committee (s.6(1)). (Act PDF pp.8, 14, 17)

An Emergency Reserve equivalent to five per cent remains unallocated for emergencies in the constituency; 'emergency' means an urgent, unforeseen need that cannot be delayed to the next financial year without harming the public interest (s.8). Project Management Committees may set aside up to 5% of a project's allocation for administration (s.9). (Act PDF p.9)

Projects must fall within the functions of the national government under the Constitution and be community-based (s.24); funds may not support political or religious bodies or activities (s.25(3)). Social security programmes, education bursary schemes, mock examinations and continuous assessment tests count as development projects but may not exceed 35% of a constituency's allocation in a year (s.48); under s.48A a Constituency Committee may, with Board approval, allocate additional funds to bursary schemes and education days. (Act PDF pp.14, 21)

Disbursement (s.39(2)): 25% of a constituency's annual allocation at the start of the first quarter, then three equal instalments at the start of the second, third and fourth quarters. All funds received under the Act are audited and reported on by the Auditor-General (s.11); the Board submits separate accounts of each constituency to the Auditor-General (s.39(4)). (Act PDF pp.9, 18)

Each constituency has an NG-CDF Committee (s.43). Its members are: the national government official responsible for coordinating national government functions; two men and two women (one of each a youth); one person with disability nominated by a registered disability group; two persons nominated by the constituency office established under the Parliamentary Service Act regulations; the Board officer seconded to the constituency (ex officio, non-voting); and one member co-opted by the Board. The names of the seven nominated members are submitted by the Board to the National Assembly for approval before appointment and gazettement (s.43(4)). (Act PDF p.19)

Role of the Member of Parliament: section 53 establishes a Constituency Oversight Committee made up of the constituency's Member of the National Assembly and not more than four other members appointed by the MP. The MP, with that committee, must convene public forums at least twice each financial year to inform the public and collect views on the Fund; oversight committee members may attend Constituency Committee meetings. The oversight committee's costs may not exceed 1% of the constituency allocation (s.53A). Two of the Constituency Committee's members are nominated by the constituency office (s.43(2)(e)). (Act PDF pp.19, 23)

According to the NG-CDF Board, the Fund is managed by the NG-CDF Board at national level, NG-CDF Committees at constituency level and Project Management Committees at community level. Constituency committees develop project proposals with residents through ward-level open forums, submit them to the Board for approval, and support the PMCs that implement projects. The Board lists ineligible projects as recurrent projects, devolved (county) functions, religious or political activities, projects that benefit individuals directly (except education bursaries and social security) and personal awards.

Legal status (as reported by the media): on 20 September 2024 a three-judge High Court bench declared the NG-CDF Act unconstitutional and ordered the Fund to stop operating at midnight on 30 June 2026. On 6 February 2026 the Court of Appeal overturned that decision and upheld the Act, but struck down section 43(9), which tied the Fund Account Manager's tenure to Parliament's term.

On 6 February 2026 the petitioners (Wanjiru Gikonyo and Cornelius Oduor Opuot) filed a notice of intention to appeal to the Supreme Court, according to Capital FM. This research did not find a Supreme Court decision as of 2026-10-25. The NG-CDF Board's data shows disbursements to all four Nyamira constituencies in August and September 2026.
